topic.title: Via Placement at SODIMM/CSODIMM/LPCAMM2 and DRAM Device Side

body.draft-comment: Go to Tools menu and click Track Changes, before you to start making any edits.

Go to Tools menu and click Accept or Reject Changes. Select Accept All in the pop-up window, before you start making edits for next revision. If the changes is common between SKUs or other platforms keep it as is to indicate it other SKU revision.
body.p: Similar to the via placement guidelines on the CPU-side, the following via placement guidelines on the DRAM-side ensure design robustness at high memory frequencies.

ul.li: Follow the Reference Validation Platform (RVP) via placement at SODIMM and Memory DRAM Down side as much as possible for all Signal Groups.
For HDI or Type-4 memory down system designs use GND Micro Vias from surface pin/pad (Top/Bottom) layer to connect to respective signal routing reference plane layers.
GND vias must be placed between signals from different signal groups and channels.

Data and Strobe vias from different byte lanes must be separated by GND vias. PTH(Plated Through Hole) via placement on the DRAM side is primarily driven by pin pitch. Follow the RVP design for optimum placement of vias.
A good example of DRAM-side ground via stitching has sufficient ground coverage for every signal in a byte lane a shown in the figure below.

Follow the via spacing guidelines covered in table below. At least one ground stitching via must be placed within every signal transition (DQ/DQS/DQS#/CLK/CTRL/CKE/CMD) whenever they change signal layers.
